value.option_title: MD verification inserted into Org-Mol's ester shortlist before synthesis
value.question: Does molecular-dynamics verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity reorder a machine-learning ester shortlist, and does the best coolant keep improving?
value.hypothesis: Molecular dynamics reorders the shortlist: machine-learning viscosity error (22.467% MAPE) exceeds molecular-dynamics error, so better esters appear after verification [s3].
held_fixed: Force field LOPLS-AA and ~15,000-atom boxes at 40 C and 1 atm [s10]
Per-candidate protocol: 3 ns equilibration plus 3 replicas of 5 ns production
The 461-monoester pool and its machine-learning ranking [s1]

predictions.if_lever: By 100 candidates the replica ranking matches the sequential baseline, diverges from machine-learning, and the best figure climbs through 1000.
predictions.if_not: Replicas match the sequential ranking only by 300 candidates; then molecular dynamics confirms the machine-learning list from 100 through 1000.
predictions.decision_rule: At 300 candidates: molecular dynamics reorders (if_lever) if the Spearman correlation between the molecular-dynamics and machine-learning rankings is below 0.7 and the best cooling figure at 300 is at least 5% higher than at 100 (ratio >= 1.05); otherwise it only confirms (if_not).
predictions.noise_rule: Ten candidates rerun at 3x length with fresh seeds; the molecular-dynamics ranking must be stable (Spearman >= 0.95 between runs), and each candidate's figure carries a block-averaged standard error across replicas.
predictions.expected_why: The machine-learning viscosity error (22.467% MAPE across a 1-12 cSt range) is large enough that molecular dynamics' closer-to-truth ranking reshuffles the top and the best figure keeps climbing.

value.compute_tested_why: Verifying more candidates is bought directly with more GPU-hours; candidate count is the varied axis, and wall-clock is compressed by running replicas and candidates side by side on the 8-GPU node.
value.scored_against: Molecular-dynamics viscosity and thermal conductivity are compared with the paper's measured Ester 1 (6.41 cSt, 0.141 W/m K) and Ester 2 (9.67 cSt, 0.138 W/m K) [s4][s5], and top candidates' cooling figure against 3M Novec 649 (0.40 cSt, 0.059 W/m K) [s13]; never against the predictors.

arms.what: Org-Mol machine-learning predicted ranking of the 461 monoesters (viscosity MAE 0.568 cSt, MAPE 22.467%), no molecular dynamics
Sequential baseline: one long single-trajectory Green-Kubo run per candidate on one A100
The method: three independent replicas per candidate on separate GPUs, block-averaged Green-Kubo integrals

baseline.what: Org-Mol's machine-learning predicted ranking of the 461 monoesters

anchor.what: Green-Kubo molecular dynamics reproduces the paper's measured Ester 1 viscosity 6.41 cSt and conductivity 0.141 W/m K.
anchor.tolerance: ±40% on viscosity and thermal conductivity (the documented LOPLS-AA error is about a factor of 1.4); parallel replicas within one standard error of the sequential run
anchor.independent_code: the sequential single-trajectory run on the same box

checks: Anchor reproduces Ester 1 (6.41 cSt, 0.141 W/m K) and Ester 2 (9.67, 0.138) within ±40%; pipeline is correct.
Each candidate's Green-Kubo integral plateaus inside the production window.
Ten candidates rerun at 3x length with new seeds; molecular-dynamics ranking stable (Spearman >= 0.95).
Top candidates' Mouromtseff figure exceeds Novec 649's; never scored against the predictors.

phases.what: Rebuild the 461 monoester SMILES from the paper's screen (dielectric < 3.20, viscosity < 12 cSt at 40 C, conductivity > 0.140 W/m K, ≤30 carbons), build ~15,000-atom boxes, assign LOPLS-AA, minimize.
phases.stop_rule: stop when 461 candidates match the paper's count and each box is equilibrated

phases.what: Green-Kubo runs of Ester 1 and Ester 2 (5 replicas x 8 ns each) plus one 24 ns sequential trajectory; measure real ns/day and the MD MAPE on the two esters; time replicas versus sequential.

gate.else: MD is no more accurate than the ML viscosity model; stop

phases.what: Top 100 candidates, 18 ns each (3 ns equilibration plus 3 x 5 ns), 8 candidates at a time.

gate.else: throughput too low to afford 300 candidates in budget; stop at top 100
the best figure already plateaued at 300; the 1000-candidate run is not justified

restructuring.sequential_part: Each candidate's viscosity waits on one long trajectory; the ranking waits on 100, 300, then 1000 candidates.
restructuring.method: Split each long trajectory into independent replicas on separate GPUs, block-average the Green-Kubo integrals, and run candidates side by side.
restructuring.condition: The replica-averaged viscosity must agree with the single-trajectory viscosity within one standard error (confirming 1/sqrt(N) replica scaling); measured on Ester 1 in the anchor phase before the main spend.
restructuring.baseline_sequential: One 24 ns single trajectory per candidate on one A100, GROMACS with -nb gpu -pme gpu -bonded gpu -update gpu -ntmpi 1, timed on the anchor esters.
restructuring.baseline_copies: Three independent replicas per candidate run side by side on separate GPUs of the 8-GPU node, timed in the anchor phase.

scope_gap: No synthesis, dielectric, flammability, material-compatibility, or long-term-stability checks; one force field and 15 ns sampling; the 1000-candidate run exceeds the $1,000 budget.

novelty.closest_prior: A 2026 benchmark ran Green-Kubo molecular dynamics on eight organic liquids; viscosity ranking stayed, thermal conductivity did not [s9][s7][s8].
novelty.left_open: Only eight molecules had viscosity and thermal conductivity Green-Kubo verified against reference values [s9]; the 100-to-1000 shortlist answer is open.

limits: Shows single-phase ranking under one force field and 15 ns sampling; no synthesis, dielectric, flammability, compatibility, or stability checks. The 1000-candidate run exceeds the budget.
value.test_summary: Run Green-Kubo molecular dynamics on the top 100 then 300 of 461 monoesters [s1]. Compare MD-vs-ML rank correlation and figure climb. Time single-trajectory against parallel replicas.

items.page_quote: "Based on the aforementioned criteria of the kinematic viscosity and thermal conductivity, 461 monoesters are finally filtered out."
items.note: Quote appears verbatim in the article; supports the 461-monoester shortlist produced by the ML-only screen.

items.page_quote: "Finally, we apply Green–Kubo MD simulations to eight molecules, two from each of the four principal chemical families of the dataset, at 40 °C and 100 °C."
items.note: Quote appears verbatim on the PMC page; supports the prior's scope of eight molecules, four chemical families, 40 and 100 °C.

items.page_quote: "Despite these limitations, the force field largely preserves the ordering of the reference viscosity values for the eight fluids at both temperatures, suggesting that MD simulations remain useful for relative screening, even where its absolute viscosity predictions require caution."
items.note: Sentence confirmed on the PMC13647254 page (Results/Discussion, MD-vs-reference viscosity comparison); supports that MD largely preserves the viscosity ranking.

items.page_quote: "Unlike the viscosity, the LOPLS force field does not reproduce even the relative ordering of the thermal conductivities of the eight fluids."
items.note: Sentence confirmed on the PMC13647254 page; supports that MD misorders the thermal conductivities.
Quote appears on the Table 4 page; experimental ν at 40°C = 6.41 cSt and experimental κ = 0.141 W/m·K for Ester 1, matching the supported claim.

items.page_quote: "For each molecule, 10 independent replicas were branched from the equilibrated configuration with independently seeded velocities... Production was carried out in the NVT ensemble for 8 ns per replica to allow the slow shear-stress autocorrelation tail to converge."
items.note: Quote appears verbatim on the PMC page; confirms the 8 ns-per-replica production protocol (with 10 replicas per molecule), supporting the compute quantity 8.
